title: Homotopy fibers of equifibered diagrams of Kan fibrations survive the diagonal
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, homotopy fibers and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. Let $X_\bullet,Y_\bullet:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$ be small simplicial diagrams of Kan complexes, and let $p:X_\bullet\to Y_\bullet$ be a natural transformation such that every $p_m:X_m\to Y_m$ is a Kan fibration. Suppose that for every $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ in $\Delta$ the naturality square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}X_n&\xrightarrow{X(\alpha)}&X_m\\ p_n\downarrow&&\downarrow p_m\\ Y_n&\xrightarrow{Y(\alpha)}&Y_m\end{array}$$
is a homotopy pullback. For $Z=X,Y$ put $(\operatorname{diag}Z)_q=(Z_q)_q$ with both operators applied simultaneously. The unique maps $[m]\to[0]$ induce maps from the constant diagrams on $X_0,Y_0$, hence maps $\iota_X:X_0\to\operatorname{diag}X$ and $\iota_Y:Y_0\to\operatorname{diag}Y$. Then
$$\begin{array}{ccc}X_0&\xrightarrow{\iota_X}&\operatorname{diag}X\\ p_0\downarrow&&\downarrow\operatorname{diag}p\\ Y_0&\xrightarrow{\iota_Y}&\operatorname{diag}Y\end{array}$$
is a homotopy pullback, naturally in $p$. Equivalently, for each vertex $y\in Y_0$, the canonical comparison from the strict fiber $p_0^{-1}(y)$ to the homotopy fiber of $\operatorname{diag}p$ at $\iota_Y(y)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Homotopy pullbacks and homotopy fibers involving a non-Kan diagonal are computed after functorial Kan replacement of the corresponding diagram. No Reedy fibrancy of the diagrams or Kan condition on their diagonals is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 6.1 and Propositions 2.2, 2.7, specialized to simplicial sets, with Remark 6.8 for rowwise equivalences; printed pp. 3-4, 11-12. The row-zero comparison follows by pulling the diagram back along the constant diagram on Y_0. Also the realization-fiber argument in Rezk, A model for the homotopy theory of homotopy theory, Section 14, pp. 33-34. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Each $p_m$ is sharp in the sense of [lem-coef-rezk-diagonal-sharp]. Indeed, let $A\to A\prime$ be any weak equivalence over $Y_m$. The map $X_m\times_{Y_m}A\to X_m\times_{Y_m}A\prime$ is the pullback of $A\to A\prime$ along $X_m\times_{Y_m}A\prime\to A\prime$. This last map is a Kan fibration: project each horn problem to $p_m$, choose its filler and pair it with the prescribed base simplex. Right properness in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] therefore makes the pullback map a weak equivalence, without any Kan assumption on $A$ or $A\prime$. The stated equivalence in [lem-coef-sharp-pullback-calculus] now says that $p_m$ is sharp.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-rezk-diagonal-sharp] to $p$. Its row maps are sharp by step 1, and all its operator squares are homotopy cartesian by hypothesis. Consequently $\operatorname{diag}p$ is sharp: its strict pullback along any map $T\to\operatorname{diag}Y$ is a homotopy pullback, even if the diagonal is not Kan.

source.place: Theorem 6.1 and Propositions 2.2, 2.7, printed pp. 3-4 and 11-12; agent reconstruction of the constant-base-change argument.

proof.text: Let $t:T\to Y_0$ be a map with $T$ Kan; later take $t=1_{Y_0}$ or a vertex $\Delta^0\to Y_0$. Write $v_m:[m]\to[0]$ for the unique map, $b_m=Y(v_m)t:T\to Y_m$, and set $G_m=X_m\times_{Y_m}T$. An operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ sends $(x,u)$ to $(X(\alpha)x,u)$, because $v_n\alpha=v_m$. These formulas give a simplicial diagram over the constant diagram on $T$. In degree $q$ its diagonal consists of pairs $(x,u)\in(X_q)_q\times T_q$ with $p_q(x)=b_q(u)$, and its operators act on both coordinates. Hence $\operatorname{diag}G=\operatorname{diag}X\times_{\operatorname{diag}Y}T$ strictly, using $T\xrightarrow{t}Y_0\xrightarrow{\iota_Y}\operatorname{diag}Y$, and $G_0=X_0\times_{Y_0}T$. These identities use only degreewise pullbacks of simplicial sets [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Theorem 6.1 and Propositions 2.2, 2.7, printed pp. 3-4 and 11-12; agent reconstruction of the constant-base-change argument.

proof.text: Fix $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ and put $P=X_m\times_{Y_m}Y_n$. Since $p_m$ is a Kan fibration, $P$ represents the homotopy pullback of this cospan, by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison]. The hypothesized homotopy-cartesian square therefore says that $e:X_n\to P$, $x\mapsto(X(\alpha)x,p_nx)$, is a weak equivalence. Both $X_n\to Y_n$ and $P\to Y_n$ are Kan fibrations: the first is $p_n$, and the second is a base change of $p_m$, whose horn-lifting property follows as in step 1. Apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-fibration-invariance] to the cospans $X_n\to Y_n\leftarrow T$ and $P\to Y_n\leftarrow T$, with comparison maps $e,1_{Y_n},1_T$ and the same map $b_n:T\to Y_n$. It gives a weak equivalence $G_n\to P\times_{Y_n}T$. By the pullback equations this target is $G_m$, and the map is exactly the operator map in step 3. Thus every structure map of $G$ is a weak equivalence; no fibration hypothesis on $b_n$ has been used.

source.place: Theorem 6.1 and Propositions 2.2, 2.7, printed pp. 3-4 and 11-12; agent reconstruction of the constant-base-change argument.

proof.text: Apply the homotopically constant clause of [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] to $G$. Step 4 verifies its hypothesis for every operator. It follows that $G_0\to\operatorname{diag}G$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Its row-$m$ map is induced by $v_m$, so under the identifications of step 3 it is $(x,u)\mapsto(X(v_m)x,u)$. In particular this is the comparison induced by $\iota_X$, rather than an unspecified equivalence.

source.place: Theorem 6.1 and Propositions 2.2, 2.7, printed pp. 3-4 and 11-12; agent reconstruction of the constant-base-change argument.

proof.text: For $T=Y_0$ and $t=1$, step 5 identifies $X_0=G_0$ by a weak equivalence with the strict pullback of $\operatorname{diag}p$ along $\iota_Y$. By step 2 that strict pullback maps by a weak equivalence to the homotopy pullback. The composite is the comparison from the square in the statement, so two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] proves that square homotopy cartesian. For $T=\Delta^0$ and $t=y$, step 5 instead gives $p_0^{-1}(y)\simeq\operatorname{diag}G$, while step 2 identifies this strict pullback with the homotopy fiber at $\iota_Y(y)$. Their composite is exactly the asserted strict-to-homotopy-fiber map. A map of natural transformations sends every pair $(x,u)$ in step 3 to the pair of its images; the formulas for $v_m$ and the projections commute with these maps. Together with the functorial diagram replacements stipulated in the statement, this proves naturality. This argument never takes a strict fiber of an arbitrary weak equivalence and never assumes the diagonals are Kan.
